title: AMD's Radeon RX 9060 XT sets new GPU frequency world record of 4.837 GHz
summary: AMD's Radeon RX 9060 XT has reached a new GPU frequency world record of 4,837 MHz. AMD VP Jack Huynh and veteran overclocker Bill Alverson used liquid nitrogen cooling to help the smaller RDNA 4 GPU open a 48MHz gap over the previous world record run.
body: AMD has set a new GPU overclocking world record by pushing the Radeon RX 9060 XT to 4,837 MHz. Veteran overclocker Bill Alverson and AMD VP Jack Huynh found the limits of this particular chip as part of a celebration of the opening of a new Micro Center location in Austin, Texas. According to the OC World Record Museum database maintained by SkatterBencher, Huynh and Alverson set the new record on November 15. If you were expecting to see this record from AMD's high-end RX 9070 XT, you're not crazy. The record was indeed achieved using the midrange RDNA 4 part rather than AMD’s flagship GPU. The RX 9060 XT uses a smaller Navi 44 GPU featuring 2,048 shading units (32 compute units), a 160W TDP, 16GB of GDDR6 memory on a 128-bit bus, and a stock boost clock speed of up to 3,130 MHz. title: 3D printer tool changers are cheaper than ever, now starting at just $599 with multiple models at lowest-ever pricing
summary: Tool-changer printers save tons of filament when printing multi-color or multi-material models, and they used to be very expensive. But not anymore, as multiple models are now on sale at or near their lowest-ever prices.
body: Tool changers — 3D printers with multiple heads — have been a major focus of the industry for more than a year, and for good reason. Multiple heads mean you don’t have to purge the nozzle every time your print swaps colors or materials, which has the dual benefit of making complex prints much faster while saving a massive amount of filament waste or “poop,” which is a problem with more traditional multi-color AMS, single-toolhead printers. 18% off Snapmaker U1 3D printer at Amazon 29% off FlashForge Creator 5 3D printer at Amazon But while these tool changers typically cost multiple thousands of dollars a few years ago, they’ve gotten much more affordable in the past year, starting with Snapmaker’s sub-$1,000 U1 ( now just $699 ) and then Fashforge’s Creator 5 not long after. And both of those printers, plus a traditional four-color AMS printer designed to minimize wasted filament, are all on sale at their lowest-ever prices as we head into Black Friday. title: Tom's Hardware’s CES 2027 Awards: How to enter your product
summary: Here’s how to submit your products for Tom's Hardware CES 2027 Awards.
body: Tom’s Hardware’s editors are inviting submissions for their CES 2027 Awards. The winners will represent bleeding-edge silicon, benchmark-busting performance, and consumer-friendly tech across several categories. We’re thrilled to spotlight the innovative products unveiled at CES 2027, happening in Las Vegas, with announcements kicking off the week of January 4. How to enter a product for consideration for a Tom's Hardware CES Award Submissions must be received by noon EST / 9 a.m. PST on Dec. 10, 2026, and the award winners will be announced during the show. To submit a product for consideration, please fill out the Tom's Hardware CES Awards submission form . Only products that are announced just before CES 2027 or that debut at the show will be considered. We are happy to sign and keep embargoes on unannounced products. If you have any questions, please email cesawards@tomshardware.com. In addition to online submissions, Tom's Hardware staff will be combing the event for new and interesting products, which will also be added to our list of nominees.
